units: 3 Troop, A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment
B Company, 5 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
B coy, 5 RAR was being moved into position as part of a Task Force attack on the VC strong-hold of the Long Hai Hills. While on a dirt track, the leading APC (carrying part of 4 pl) hit a powerful mine resulting in the two cavalrymen being killed, and two infantry. The rest of the troops in the APC were severely wounded. The APC was thrown on its side and the crater was 1m deep and 2m wide. 

The rest of the Tp immediately slewed left and right in a counter ambush procedure. Once it was clear no ambush was occurring, infantry officers and men jumped off their APCs and ran to assist the medics already attending the dead and wounded. They set off more M16 anti-personnel mines. Most of the medics and the Coy HQ were either killed or wounded. Normal mine-contact procedures had been ignored. Engineers ordered everyone to keep still while they cleared the mines. Medical support was sent in by Helo.

Operation Renmark was cancelled. 

Location was the Long Hais.
notable.archivalSource: AWM279 569/R4/37; When the Scorpion Stings pg55; On the Offensive pg121; AWM95 7-5-15.pdf 5 RAR Mar 67 pg158;

units: 11 Platoon, D Company, 5 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
12 Platoon, D Company, 6 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
9 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
6 enemy fired RPG from a bunker system at 11 pl 1250hrs. Enemy was quickly reinforced to squad size. Camp had 21 bunkers in an area of 200x200 metres. While it was withdrawing, 12 pl were fired on by RPGs 1447hrs. D coy withdrew and the camp was attacked with arty and 2 airstrikes and LFT. D coy returned to the undefended camp the next day. 12 pl thought that it had killed 3 en and 11 pl had killed 2.

See Combined Arms Data Base


D Coy, 11 pl,12 pl, were moving W with 11 pl leading. 11 pl leading elements heard movement 20 - 30m to their S and then they were fired upon. They returned the fire. 12 pl were moved S 100m then swept from E to W (1220hrs). When they were due S of 11 pl they contacted enemy in bunkers firing SA. 12 pl engaged and held in that location. 11 pl whilst attempting to clear the ground between themselves and 12 pl were fired on by 6 en with RPGs.(1250hrs) and sustained 1 casualty.  It was realised the system was larger than initially suspected so C/S42 were withdrawn E to evacuate their cas covered by 12 pl. As soon as DUSTOFF hovered 12 pl was fired upon by HMG, RPG and SA. The helicopter were fired upon and forced to depart without the casualty. 
  12 pl suffered 5 cas in the engagement and when 11 pl DUSTOFF was complete 12 pl withdrew E to effect their own cas evac.

The OC of D Coy observed that no manouvering of subunits should take place when a bunker system is suspected, until careful and thorough examination of the ground has taken place. The enemy has excellent fire discipline and will lie quietly for hours only 20m away awaiting his best opportunity. The enemy will hold fire until a dustoff helo is just hovering and at its most vulnerable moment. Do not be sucked in to a bunker engagement unless heavy arty and air support and tanks are available. Enemy returned to collect bodies although 4 were found 2 days later. The M72 was not able to be used as effectively as the RPG. The enemy had prepared bunkers to take RPG back blast, but foliage was too dense for M72 back blast. The enemy had also cut fire lanes for the RPG, there were none for the M72 because the ground was chosen by the enemy. The RPG was more effective in dense bush because with its system of inertial ignition, it does not ignite on hitting small twigs and undergrowth. The M72 has a graze fuse with bakelite cap, point ignition and base detonation. It is much more sensitive to foliage.
notable.archivalSource: Intsum, AWM95 1/4/140.pdf p73; AWM 290 item 9/25 op. Goodwood; AWM95 7-9-11.pdf 9 RAR Feb 69 pg174-179; AWM95 7-9-12.pdf 9 RAR Feb 69 pg196 Contact Rept;

notable.report:
11 pl contacts pl of enemy in bunker system. 11 Platoon was spread out along the objective when fire opened and found that all elements of the  platoon were under fire. This meant that the platoon commander had no reserve to use to extract his platoon.  Heavy casualties suffered. Pl hit by claymores and heavy small arms fire and RPGs. RPG fire killed one man and wounded 7 (this contact report). Arty, called in. At 1106hrs 12 pl entered the area as did LTF called in as well as airstrikes.(See 910hrs). 11 pl able to disengage and carry out wounded. In contact for 4 hrs. Arty failed to  contribute effectively to the contact.

notable.report:
A Coy of 1 Bn, 33 Regt NVA attacked Duc Trung and overwhelmed the local defense pl. B coy sent to recover the situation. Initially Arty fire was brought down to within 20m of the houses causing enemy casualties. This was supported by an LFT which attacked on the N and W sides of the village. B coy then attacked the S of the village with 1 tp of tanks. The enemy was routed, and the PF took over the clearance of the rest of the village to avoid civilian casualties.

See Combined Arms Data Base

units: 1 Company, 52 Battalion, Army of the Republic of Vietnam
2 Company, 52 Battalion, Army of the Republic of Vietnam
3 Platoon, A Company, 5 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
Force was 10 Aust and 55 ARVN soldiers.

The combined force of 10 Aust and 55 ARVN had conducted an ambush (see 1415hrs) and had dusted off their wounded. The patrol was moving to a new ambush site when it was attacked by a platoon of MF VC with heavy fire from AK47s, M79s and RPGs. The Aust led force was receiving fire from all directions but could get no arty support because of poor comms. Finally, a possum aircraft relayed the requests and arty began to land in the area. But the enemy closed up on the Aust force to avoid the arty. However, 2xLFTs arrived and gave fire support to within 25m of the Aust force. The enemy decided to withdraw. The Aust/ARVN force suffered 7 ARVN wded all caused by RPGs. Enemy suffered 2 killed with 6 possible from many blood trails. These were caused by SA, arty and LFTs.
notable.archivalSource: AWM288 459/1/2/2 pt3 After Action Reports 5 RAR 66-69; AWM95 7-5-31.pdf pg10 Contact Rept;

units: 12 Platoon, D Company, 5 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
Enemy moved along track from South to North. Platoon was in 1/2 Platoon groups 70 metres apart. The enemy moved through the southern group to the northern group. The northern group opened fire when leading elements were in their killing ground. The enemy were still moving through the southern group and the southern group opened fire on them. To this stage 45 enemy had been counted and they were still coming when fire opened. The enemy withdrew hastily east and south east without returning fire. Some elements dragged bodies out and assisted casualties, the movement and noise could be heard and was fired on each time. When it was light enough a sweep was done, preceded by clearing by fire. Gun ships were used 200 metres to the east, south east and south plus artillery and mortars in depth. 5 AK47 captured. 1 Aust wded by shrap to head from en grenade, remained on duty.

Intsum: YS315821, 12/D/5 RAR contacts about 45 enemy moving N. 7 en killed, 5 en killed poss, 9 en wded (BT and drag marks). 5 AK47, 1xpistol, 2xclaymore, 5xrifle grens, 13 AK47 mags, 450 SAA rds, 10xpacks of food and rice, and docs captured.

105 Fd Bty fired 100 rds in support (AWM95 3/6/17.pdf p8 1 Fd Regt Diary)
notable.archivalSource: Contact Report AWM288, item R459/1/2/2 Part 1, After action Reports

Light Fire Team
notable.report:
On hearing voices a short distance ahead, Aslt Pnr pl called up 3 pl and they launched a two pl assault on enemy bunker system. Artillery was fired behind bunker system to act as a cutoff. 3 pl opened fire on enemy in open, but was met  by  very heavy RPG and AK47 fire from bunkers and flanks. RPG rounds were also landing in rear of pls causing casualties. Aslt Pnr covered retreat of 3 pl to a base 30m from bunkers. LFTs were now firing in support of pls. As dustoff helos appeared they became targets for enemy who closed up on base and fired 60mm Mortars, SA and RPGs which landed amongst the wounded in the base perimeter creating more wounded. LFTs suppressed this fire and base was moved away to allow safe evacuation of wounded.

See Combined Arms Data Base

Further to contact of 211605H at YS245827. Original contact was made by Aslt Pnr pl and 3 Pl. The Aslt Pnr Pl was preparing a harbour position when they heard noises approx 300m away. The area was engaged by 105 Fd Bty with 72 rds of 105mm delay fuze. The 2 pls with Aslt Pnr Pl leading and command by 2IC A Coy moved into the contact area. The Pnr Pl was engaged by enemy SA and RPG fire and received approx 6 casualties. 3 Pl formed a firm fire base and the Aslt Pnr Pl withdrew. The whole group was engaged by SA and RPG fire from flank and 2 flanks. 10 casualties were sustained during this period. The group then withdrew to a clear area for DUSTOFF. Whilst DUSTOFF was in progress a large enemy force counter attack from flank using fire and movement. Most casualties were sustained during this period. At least 10 enemy were seen to fall during the contact. Consolidated figures to date are : 10 VC KIA (POSS), 4 VC KBA, 1 Aust KIA, 31 Aust WIA (evacuated).

Coy OC coments was that the Coy comms net was a shambles with every element supporting the contact having a say. He suggested that a FAC be on the Coy net and that he should control all air on a separate net.

AWM95 7-5-34.pdf pg186 The cas for this were amended to 9 en killed, 4 en killed by Arty/air, 25 en wded.
